main_text.p: Idem quedam esse femina testatur, quæ partim in hordei aut typha, partim in typhæ oly ræ aut tritici medio sunt loco, quædam vero esse quæ ad olyræ, alia ad hordei aut typhæ, alia ad tritici, alia ad panici, alia quæ ad milii naturam proxime accedant quæ nomina habent, alia simplicia, ut in Italia, alia composita, ut in Cappadocia ψυμνόκεφρον[?], hoc est, hordeum nudum ac corticis expers. In Bithynia autem minoris Asiæ regione Zeopyron, hoc est, ex Zea quod tritico nomen conflatum est, ut ita adeo differant, ut ei non nisi ad ea, quæ sunt ex tritico, quo nomen maius est, de eis feminibus exquisite differre.

Quidam Galeniinte pretes Chondrum far verterunt, ut Linacer vir utraque literatura clarissimus. Quid hoc die fit pa-um coffare vi- deo. Ruellius scribit in Gallia farris duo genera: Var., rafe ut vn- ma rutilo colore, arufitus agricola lis rutilum frumentum appellatum, ge. man. Kerni alte um candidum, quod clam finum purum tatur, germ. Spelt oder Dinckel, Columella farris 4, descriptgenera, Venuculum rutilum, venuculum album germ. Teutsch Reiß/ryage manica, clusinum gen. Spelt/ zimen, deniq, trimeftre alias halcaft um, germanis Ammelkorn / quod pondere bonitatem, pracipuum est: unde non cadit illorum fententia, quæ Chondron, hoc est alicam & far adoreum Co- lamella,

page.notes: The Greek word "ψυμνόκεφρον" is doubtful and marked [?]. Several German words are in black letter and marked by <bl>-style intent in the text, but not all could be read with certainty; the lines around "Kerni", "Spelt oder Dinckel" and "Ammelkorn" are the least certain. The marginal note "Varie opiniones de farre." sits beside the lines about spelt, the note "Var." beside the paragraph's second block. Some words in the second block are blurred and are transcribed on best reading.
